newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS - Wall Street surge pulls Euro shares higher.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Wall Street surge pulls Euro shares higher.

text.p: European shares followed U.S. stocks higher again on Friday when Wall Street took a positive view of a key economic indicator showing that the world's number one economy was still generating new jobs at a stunning rate.
U.S. non-farm payrolls rose by a huge 339,000 in February, the most since May, when payrolls rose by 247,000. Economists polled in a Reuters survey had expected a 230,000-job gain.

"The numbers were unambiguously strong (but the report is)... not going to prompt a March move (to tighten U.S. interest rates)," Wayne Ayers, chief economist at the Bank of Boston, told Reuters Financial Television.

Share traders on both sides of the Atlantic fear that a move by the U.S. Federal Reserve to raise interest rates to cap inflation could sorely test a global bull market in shares which has seen prices surge to record after record recently

"This report does not change things dramatically in terms of Fed policy. The main strength was in construction, which the Labor Department tied to mild weather. The hourly earnings data, (up three cents to $12.09 in February) didn't cause much of a scare," David Sloan, senior economist at I.D.E.A. INC, said.

The benchmark 30-year U.S. Treasury bond fell immediately after the report but then rebounded, adding a third of a point. Its yield eased to 6.86 percent from Thursday's 6.88, giving the green light to further gains for U.S. shares.
Shortly after European boures closed, the Dow Jones index of U.S. blue chip shares was up 60.42 points at 7,005.12, or around 0.85 percent.
In London, the FTSE index closed up 21 points at 4,420.3, a new record close, while in Paris the CAC-40 index was up 9.36 points at 2,708.28, which was also a new record close.
Germany's DAX fell 41.40 points to 3,376.2 but had closed floor trade before the U.S. jobs figures were released. In post-bourse trading the Ibis DAX index was up 22.96 points at 3,419.51.
But some strategists said that both the U.S. and British markets could come under pressure in the near term as fears grow of fiscal tightening in both countries.
Higher interest rates would be bad news for share prices by making the cost of borrowing more expensive for companies and alternative investments more attractive to investors.
Any selloff in U.S. share prices, which are at record levels, would undermine European share prices, too.
"The first reaction to figures is usually the wrong one," said Richard Kersley, strategist at BZW.

However, the day's bullish mood was captured by one London trader who said, "With the Dow now looking like it could set a new record, some people are taking the view that they'd better fill their boots (with shares)."
Friday's rise meant London's FTSE had risen 112 points, or 2.6 percent, during the week and by 302 points, or 7.3 percent, so far this year.

Paris stocks also shrugged off the stronger-than-expected U.S. jobs growth to set a third consecutive closing record on Friday. The jobs data briefly unsettled the market but French shares recovered from their lows to push higher.

The blue-chip CAC-40 index hit a historic intraday high of 2,718.95. A senior equity salesman at a French broker said the market took heart from a January U.S. employment figure which was revised down to 247,000 from an initial 271,000.
Germany's 30-share blue-chip DAX index ended bourse trading sharply lower with traders in Frankfurt seeking inspiration to give direction and cure a hangover from the record run of recent days.

In currencies, the dollar motored back to 34-month highs against the mark after the U.S jobs figures but settled off peaks in Europe as the figures failed to convince the market of an imminent rate hike. It was still up, however, from its late European level on Thursday.

"The employment numbers are pretty good...On the other hand, they are not strong enough to give the market a view the Fed will definitely be tightening rates," said Tony Norfield, treasury economist at ABN AMR0.
Against the yen, the dollar climbed to session peaks at 122.12 but retrenched, though it remained up from Thursday's late level.
CURRENCIES AT 1700 GMT
The dollar was quoted around 1.71673 marks and 121.85 yen, compared with 1.7168 and 121.20 late on Thursday.
STOCK MARKETS CLOSING PRICES
LONDON - The FTSE-100 index was up 21 points, or 0.48 percent, at 4,420.3.
PARIS - The CAC-40 was up 9.36 points, or 0.35 percent, at 2,708.28.
FRANKFURT - The 30-share DAX index closed down 41.40 points at 3,376.20. The DAD-Ibis index of post-bourse trading closed up 22.96, or 0.68 percent, at 3,419.51.
PRECIOUS METALS
Gold stood at $349.05 at the London close, compared $352.20 late on Thursday.
